terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the catalogue, the stock and the settings turned into text and back.

tasks.title: Save the catalogue as text
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/saving.js`, make `saveCatalogue(candles)` return the list as JSON text, indented by two spaces so Theo can read the file. The list stays as it is.

Check calls `saveCatalogue` with lists of its own, an empty one included, and compares the text letter by letter.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on turning data into text.
Turn the list into JSON text.
Ask for two spaces of indent.
Run the file: each property should be on a line of its own.
hints: `String(candles)` and template literals turn objects into `[object Object]`. JSON keeps what is inside.
`JSON.stringify` takes the value first. Its third value is the indent; the second can be `null`.
The function is one line: `return JSON.stringify(candles, null, 2)`.

tasks.title: Load it back, even when it is broken
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `loadCatalogue(text)` return the list that `text` holds. When `text` is not JSON, because the file was cut off or someone typed in it, it returns an empty list instead of stopping. Check only gives it the text of a saved list, or broken text.

Check calls `loadCatalogue` with saved lists, a cut off file, an empty file and text that is not JSON at all.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on reading JSON and on broken text.
Turn the text back into a list.
Put that inside a `try`, and give back an empty list in its `catch`.
Run the file: the second line for Task 2 should be an empty list, not an error.
hints: `JSON.parse` reads JSON text back into data, and throws an error on text it cannot read.
An error inside `try { }` does not stop the program: Node jumps to the `catch { }` part, and the function can give back something else from there.
The body has the shape `try { return JSON.parse(text) } catch { return [] }`.

tasks.title: Save the stock Map and bring it back
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `saveStock(stock)` return JSON text that keeps every entry of `stock`, a `Map` from sku to count. Then make `loadStock(text)` take text that `saveStock` made and return a `Map` with the same entries.

Check saves Maps of its own with your `saveStock`, an empty one included, makes sure the text keeps every entry, then loads that text with your `loadStock` and compares the Map it gives with the one it started from.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on what does not survive the trip.
In `saveStock`, turn the Map into something JSON keeps, then into JSON text.
In `loadStock`, read the text back and turn what you get into a Map.
Run the file: the last line for Task 3 should be a Map again.
hints: `JSON.stringify` on a Map gives `{}`: its entries are not properties, so JSON leaves them out.
Spread turns a Map into a list of `[key, value]` pairs, and JSON keeps lists. `new Map()` takes such a list and makes a Map from it.
`saveStock` is `return JSON.stringify([...stock])`, and `loadStock` is `return new Map(JSON.parse(text))`.

tasks.title: Load the settings with defaults
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, first write a function of your own called `readJson`, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It has two parameters, `text` and `fallback`, and returns the value `text` holds as JSON, or `fallback` when `text` is not JSON. A value that counts as false, such as `0` or `null`, is still JSON. It only helps `loadSettings`, so it stays off the `export` line.

Then make `loadSettings(text)` return a new object with every setting of `defaultSettings`, and over them every setting saved in `text`, which may be only some of them. When `text` is not JSON, it returns the defaults. Use `readJson` to read the text. `defaultSettings` stays as it is. Check only gives it the text of a saved settings object, or broken text.

Check calls `readJson` and `loadSettings` with texts of its own, makes sure `defaultSettings` is unchanged afterwards, and reads your file for `readJson` and the call to it inside `loadSettings`.
nextSteps: Above `loadSettings`, write `function readJson(text, fallback) {` and its closing `}` yourself.
Make it give back what the text holds, or the fallback when reading it throws.
In `loadSettings`, make a new object with the defaults, then the saved settings over them.
Run the file: the broken text should give the default settings.
hints: `readJson` is `loadCatalogue` from Task 2 with the fallback as a parameter.
Spreading two objects into a new one copies both; when a key appears twice, the one written last wins. An empty object is a handy fallback, since spreading it adds nothing.
`readJson` is `try { return JSON.parse(text) } catch { return fallback }`, and `loadSettings` is `return { ...defaultSettings, ...readJson(text, {}) }`.
